description:
The existing simulation pipeline uses the generic checkpoint form, with its recorded crash-safety behaviour demonstrated unchanged.

## Background

The checkpoint mechanism's behaviour is pinned by two tests: a resume-versus-uninterrupted counter-equality test and a signal-and-resume byte-identity subprocess test. Genericising the writer and reader must not disturb the one caller that exists — the modulation campaign binary — and the demonstration that it does not is this leaf's deliverable: the caller moves onto the generic form and both pinned tests pass with their assertions unchanged.

Migration is separate from the foundation because the two are independently reviewable: the foundation's fresh-payload round-trip shows the mechanism has one form, and this migration shows the existing consumer kept its behaviour.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The existing simulation pipeline uses the generic checkpoint form, with the previously hard-coded payload as one instantiation and no campaign-specific code left in the checkpoint module.
- [hard] REQ-02: The resume-versus-uninterrupted counter-equality test and the signal-and-resume byte-identity subprocess test pass with their assertions unchanged.

## Notes

Scope is the caller migration and its regression demonstration alone; the generic mechanism lands ahead of this leaf on its dependency edge.
title: Existing pipeline migrated onto the generic checkpoint
